confidence_legend.estimate: my calculation or inference, never a published figure

design_targets.woofer: 12 in, centre z 320, ~88 L net vented, f3 near 32 Hz; drawn frame dia ~310 (spec), flush in a rebate under a 3 mm satin black trim ring with 0.8 mm reveal; owner wants the frame ~52 mm clear of the plinth shadow line (z 113) -> frame <= ~314 mm keeps that
design_targets.mid: 6.5 in, centre z 690, sealed sub-chamber (~8 L PROPOSAL, 90 mm clear depth behind the baffle); drawn frame dia ~170
design_targets.tweeter: 1 in dome at the throat of an oblate-spheroidal waveguide carved into the 37.6 deg slope; axis z 903.5, faceplate plane y 125 (SPEC 2026-10-08)
design_targets.crossover: label says 350 Hz and 2.2 kHz; active (Hypex DSP plate amp) likely, tweeter crossover anywhere ~1.5-3 kHz

gable_geometry_constraint_for_tweeter.rule: anything coaxial in the throat plane (a visible faceplate, or a hidden flange just behind a thin throat ring) must stay within ~80-81 mm diameter to keep ~3 mm of birch over the body's top panel (floor-limited); the roof allows ~89 mm
gable_geometry_constraint_for_tweeter.consequence: 100-104 mm faceplates (SB26 family, Seas 27TBFC/G, Scan-Speak D2608/D2604, Peerless DX25/XT25BG60, Satori TW29 as sold, Purifi WG104) do not fit at the spec axis unless removed or trimmed, or unless the tweeter moves >= ~10 mm further back AND its pocket cuts ~7-9 mm into the 18 mm top panel (both spec changes)
gable_geometry_constraint_for_tweeter.method: estimate from spec/geometry.md and fab/params.py: body top z 860, axis z 903.5, slope z = 860 + 0.7701 y

recommended.label: Active POC (Hypex FusionAmp FA253 per speaker)
recommended.crossover: LR4 ~300-350 Hz and ~2.0 kHz (1.8-2.4 to taste) in the FA253's DSP; EQ the woofer's 37 Hz bump; time-align the tweeter (it sits ~0.24 ms late at 125 mm setback)
why: woofer and mid keep the drawn frame sizes (314 vs ~310, 165 vs ~170), so the outside does not change
RSS315HF-4: ~6 dB more clean output than the DSA315-8 (Vd 736 vs 279 cm3) and a 4 ohm load that suits the FA253's 250 W channel
MR16P-8: a real midrange (Le 0.11 mH, 32-8000 Hz) with a dark papyrus cone close to the renders' charcoal paper

TW29DN-B: the only buyable 1 in-class dome found whose maker documents taking the faceplate off for a waveguide, so the carved wall meets the surround with no flat ring; Fs ~650 Hz and 80 W allow ~2 kHz
recommended.buy_first: one TW29DN-B for the gable test slice; design the waveguide around its measured diaphragm

alternate.label: Passive-capable, lower cost
alternate.crossover: passive 350 Hz / 2.2 kHz works (tweeter Fs 425-440 Hz); active ~1.6-2 kHz also possible
why: no CAD change for the woofer (the 272 cutout placeholder) and the mid frame equals the drawn 170
DS315-8 is flat in 88 L at fb 32 Hz with no EQ
D3004/602200 has the lowest Fs of any tweeter that fits the gable and seats in the existing 62 mm faceplate pocket

faceplate.removable_how: SB's WG29-187 mounting sheet (rev 0, 2026-03-18): remove the faceplate screws (2.5 mm hex key), lift the faceplate slowly (adhesive at the diaphragm rim can stick to its back), refit the same screws through SB's adapter ring; the waveguide slips into the ring and locks with 4 set screws (1.3 mm hex)
faceplate.element_variant: no separate element SKU; factory waveguide versions exist (TW29BNWG, TW29TXNWG with a 170 mm aluminium waveguide) and the WG29-187 waveguide accessory fits all TW29 models (per SB/retailers)

mounting.screw: 2.5 mm hex socket -> likely M3 socket cap or M4 button head (unconfirmed)
mounting.rear_mount: with the faceplate off the motor/diaphragm unit has the faceplate screw holes facing forward. Option A (suggested): a printed or turned throat ring that forms the first few mm of the OS wall, screwed to the motor with those screws as SB's adapter ring is, the module inserted from the front into brass inserts in the birch so the joint falls just outside the surround. Option B: SB's own adapter ring (comes with the WG29-187) seated in a counterbore. Body no wider than the 71-74 mm cutout, ~32 mm deep -> fits the <=80 mm limit at the spec axis
